This section examines Experiment R —
Transfer-guided evaluation from first

principles. Keep two questions separate:
does changing the order change

the measured outcome, and does the
proposed search method beat

a matched alternative at the same
distinct-evaluation budget? Input: the

complete six-module source landscape and
222 cached eight-module candidates.

Correlations: Spearman approximately 0.656
and Pearson 0.685 in the final

cached policy analysis. Guided order: rank
candidates using the transferred

score, not their true target fitness.
Outcome: a perfect eight-module

ordering was found by budget five. Random
probability: 0.248 of

at least one perfect hit by budget five
because 12/222

candidates were perfect. Top 10%
transferred candidates: mean target

accuracy 0.900 versus 0.725 for the pool.
Caveat: optima were

not sparse, so this is supporting evidence
rather than a

standalone top-tier result. Now read
evidence panel R-guided. The axes,
